// File: main.tf
# This rds.tf must be replaced by a module for each RDS instance.
resource "aws_db_instance" "dbinstances" {
  for_each = var.rds_instances

  identifier                  = each.value.db_instance_identifier
  instance_class              = each.value.db_instance_class

  storage_type                = lookup(each.value, "storage_type", "gp2")
  allocated_storage           = each.value.allocated_storage
  max_allocated_storage       = lookup(each.value, "max_allocated_storage", null)

  engine                      = each.value.engine
  engine_version              = each.value.engine_version
  license_model               = lookup(each.value, "license_model", null)

  username                    = lookup(each.value, "master_username", "master")
  password                    = each.value.master_password
  db_name                     = each.value.db_name

  vpc_security_group_ids      = lookup(each.value, "vpc_security_group_ids", null)
  publicly_accessible         = lookup(each.value, "publicly_accessible", false)

  allow_major_version_upgrade = lookup(each.value, "allow_major_version_upgrade", false)
  auto_minor_version_upgrade  = lookup(each.value, "auto_minor_version_upgrade", false)

  copy_tags_to_snapshot       = lookup(each.value, "copy_tags_to_snapshot", true)
  multi_az                    = lookup(each.value, "multi_az", false)
}

resource "aws_rds_cluster" "dbclusters" {
  for_each = var.rds_clusters

  allocated_storage           = each.value.allocated_storage
  storage_type                = each.value.storage_type
  availability_zones          = each.value.availability_zones
  allow_major_version_upgrade = each.value.allow_major_version_upgrade
  cluster_identifier          = each.value.cluster_identifier
  cluster_identifier_prefix   = each.value.cluster_identifier_prefix
  copy_tags_to_snapshot       = each.value.copy_tags_to_snapshot
  database_name               = each.value.database_name
  db_cluster_instance_class   = each.value.db_cluster_instance_class
  deletion_protection         = each.value.deletion_protection
  engine                      = each.value.engine
  engine_mode                 = each.value.engine_mode
  engine_version              = each.value.engine_version
  global_cluster_identifier   = each.value.global_cluster_identifier
  iam_roles                   = each.value.iam_roles
  iops                        = each.value.iops
  master_password             = each.value.master_password
  master_username             = each.value.master_username
  vpc_security_group_ids      = each.value.vpc_security_group_ids

  dynamic "scaling_configuration" {
    for_each = each.value.engine_mode == "serverless" ? [1] : []

    content {
      auto_pause               = each.value.scaling_configuration.auto_pause
      max_capacity             = each.value.scaling_configuration.max_capacity
      min_capacity             = each.value.scaling_configuration.min_capacity
      timeout_action           = each.value.scaling_configuration.timeout_action
      seconds_until_auto_pause = each.value.scaling_configuration.seconds_until_auto_pause
    }
  }

  dynamic "serverlessv2_scaling_configuration" {
    for_each = each.value.engine_mode == "provisioned" ? [1] : []

    content {
      max_capacity             = each.value.scaling_configuration.max_capacity
      min_capacity             = each.value.scaling_configuration.min_capacity
    }
  }
}

// File: output.tf
output "RDSInstances" {
   value = toset([
    for dbinstance in aws_db_instance.dbinstances : 
    {
      "db_instance_identifier" = dbinstance.db_instance_identifier,
      "engine" = dbinstance.engine,
      "engine_version" = dbinstance.engine_version,
      "master_username" = dbinstance.master_username,
      "db_name" = dbinstance.db_name,
      "multi_az" = dbinstance.multi_az,
      "endpoint" = dbinstance.address
    }
  ])
}

output "RDSClusters" {
  value = toset([
    for dbcluster in aws_rds_cluster.dbclusters :
    {
      "cluster_identifier" = dbcluster.cluster_identifier,
      "engine" = dbcluster.engine,
      "engine_version" = dbcluster.engine_version,
      "master_username" = dbcluster.master_username,
      "db_name" = dbcluster.database_name,
      "availability_zones" = dbcluster.availability_zones,
      "endpoint" = dbcluster.endpoint
    }
  ])
}

output "DefaultTags" {
  value = var.tags
}

variable "rds_instances" {
  description = "Map os values for multiple RDS instances"
  type = map(
    object({

      allocated_storage           = number

      storage_type                = string
      engine                      = string

      cluster_identifier_prefix   = string
      cluster_identifier          = string

It must define three subnets with configurable CIDR blocks, availability zones, public IP mapping flags, and name tags, defaulting as follows: Subnet A with CIDR "10.0.1.0/24", the first availability zone in the region, public IP mapping true, and name "Subnet-A-Public"; Subnet B with CIDR "10.0.2.0/24", the second availability zone in the region, public IP mapping false, and name "Subnet-B-Private"; and Subnet C with CIDR "10.0.3.0/24", a third, distinct availability zone in the region, public IP mapping false, and name "Subnet-C-Private". The VPC must enable DNS support and hostnames, attach the tagged Internet Gateway, and include a route table tagged with the route table name that contains a default route targeting "0.0.0.0/0" via the Internet Gateway, associated explicitly only with Subnet A. Additionally, provision a VPC-scoped Elastic IP using the configured BYOIP IPv4 pool to deploy a NAT gateway tagged with the NAT gateway name inside Subnet B with an explicit dependency on the Internet Gateway, alongside a custom security group named "DefaultSecurityGroup" within the VPC that permits all outbound egress traffic.

user_prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a complete AWS Backup solution with automated multi-tiered backup plans, resource selection rules, IAM permissions, and optional notification configurations for enterprise backup management. The infrastructure must provision a KMS key with key rotation enabled to encrypt an AWS Backup vault whose name defaults to "my-backup-vault", accepting optional resource tags. It must set up an IAM role assumed by backup.amazonaws.com attached to the managed AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup policy to execute backup operations. The template must construct three distinct backup plans named after the vault with suffixes "-daily", "-weekly", and "-monthly"—each containing an advanced backup setting enabling WindowsVSS for EC2 resources, along with corresponding backup selections named "daily_backup_selection", "weekly_backup_selection", and "monthly_backup_selection" targeting all resources ("*") matching string-like tag conditions on a configurable tag key defaulting to "backup" for values "daily", "weekly", and "monthly", respectively. The daily backup plan rule ("daily_backup_rule") must use a default schedule of "cron(0 12 ? * * *)", a lifecycle deletion threshold of 7 days, and an optional continuous backup flag defaulting to false; the weekly backup plan rule ("weekly_backup_rule") must use a default schedule of "cron(0 12 ? * 1 *)" and a lifecycle deletion threshold of 31 days; and the monthly backup plan rule ("monthly_backup_rule") must use a default schedule of "cron(0 12 1 * ? *)" and a lifecycle deletion threshold of 366 days. Finally, the template must conditionally provision backup vault notifications controlled by a boolean flag defaulting to false, sending alerts to a specified SNS topic ARN for a configurable event list defaulting to BACKUP_JOB_FAILED, RESTORE_JOB_FAILED, COPY_JOB_FAILED, S3_BACKUP_OBJECT_FAILED, and S3_RESTORE_OBJECT_FAILED.

user_prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a multi-AZ highly available VPC network architecture with redundant NAT gateways for testing environment deployments. The template must configure input variables for an AWS region defaulting to "us-east-1", an environment tag ("env") defaulting to "test", a VPC CIDR defaulting to "10.0.0.0/16", public subnet CIDRs defaulting to ["10.0.10.0/24", "10.0.11.0/24"], private subnet CIDRs defaulting to ["10.0.20.0/24", "10.0.21.0/24"], and common tags containing an Owner of "Valerii Vasianovych" and Project of "Terraform AWS". The VPC must be named using the environment tag value followed by "-vpc", carry a custom tag recording the current AWS region merged with the common tags, and attach an Internet Gateway named using the environment tag value followed by "-igw". Public subnets must map public IPs on launch, be spread across the available availability zones in the region, be named using the environment tag value followed by "-public-subnet-" and a sequential index, and route default internet traffic ("0.0.0.0/0") through a single shared public route table named using the environment tag value followed by "-route-public-subnets". Additionally, the template must provision dedicated Elastic IPs and NAT Gateways matching the count of private subnets, placed inside the corresponding public subnets and named using the environment tag value followed by "-nat-eip-" and "-nat-gw-" plus a sequential index, paired with separate private route tables named using the environment tag value followed by "-route-private-subnets-" plus a sequential index that route outbound traffic to their respective NAT Gateway, for private subnets named using the environment tag value followed by "-private-subnet-" plus a sequential index.

We need a Terraform template that creates a conditionally deployed Amazon EKS cluster along with its required IAM service role to host containerized workloads. The infrastructure must set up an IAM role named "eks-cluster" assumed by the "eks.amazonaws.com" service principal, attached to both the managed AmazonEKSClusterPolicy and AmazonEKSVPCResourceController policies. The EKS cluster resource itself must be conditionally created based on a boolean variable named create_eks defaulting to false, configured with configurable variables for cluster_name defaulting to an empty string, cluster_version defaulting to null, and authentication_mode defaulting to "API_AND_CONFIG_MAP" while explicitly setting bootstrap_cluster_creator_admin_permissions to true. For network placement, the cluster VPC configuration must dynamically evaluate subnet options by selecting control_plane_subnet_ids if populated, otherwise falling back to subnet_ids, with both list variables defaulting to empty. Finally, enforce explicit dependencies to ensure the cluster waits for both IAM role policy attachments before creation and releases them only after cluster destruction.

user_prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates environment-specific IAM service accounts and access credentials for CI/CD integration across development, testing, and production environments. The stack must deploy three IAM users named "DevUser-rwwise.dev", "TestUser-rwwise.dev", and "ProdUser-rwwise.dev", each configured under the path "/system/" and tagged with a Name of "rwwise.dev Infrastructure Setup", Repository of "https://github.com/zangrum/setup.inf.rwwise.dev", and dynamic account and user IDs fetched from the current AWS caller identity context. Every user must have an active IAM access key generated alongside a dedicated inline user policy named "dev_cicd_user_policy", "test_cicd_user_policy", and "prod_cicd_user_policy", respectively. The policy documents attached to all three users must contain identical statements granting: read-only/list access to CodeBuild, CodeCommit, CloudWatch metrics, EventBridge rules/targets, and CloudWatch logs across all resources; CodeStar Connections connection lookup permissions for "arn:aws:codestar-connections:::connection/" under statement ID "CodeStarConnectionsUserAccess"; CodeStar Notifications rule description for all resources constrained by a StringLike condition on "codestar-notifications:NotificationsForResource" matching "arn:aws:codebuild:" under statement ID "CodeStarNotificationsPowerUserAccess"; and general listing access for CodeStar Notification rules, event types, and targets under statement ID "CodeStarNotificationsListAccess".

We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive, modular Amazon SNS messaging architecture including topics, standalone topic policies, endpoint subscriptions, SMS account preferences, and mobile platform applications. Global prefix variables for name ("TEST") and environment ("STAGE") must construct default lowercased resource names or display names when explicit values are not provided, and resource creation across components must be controlled by individual boolean flags defaulting to false: enable_sns_topic, enable_sns_topic_policy, enable_sns_topic_subscription, enable_sns_sms_preferences, and enable_sns_platform_application. The SNS topic component must accept mutually exclusive name or name_prefix settings, custom display names (defaulting to "lower(var.name)-sns-{lower(var.environment)}"), inline delivery or access policies, KMS encryption key IDs, and configurable success/failure feedback IAM roles and sample rates for application, HTTP, Lambda, and SQS protocols, while applying a create_before_destroy lifecycle policy. The standalone topic policy component must require a JSON policy document and automatically fall back to referencing the created SNS topic ARN if an explicit topic ARN is not provided. The subscription component must iterate over a list of endpoint strings, defaulting the protocol to "sqs", confirmation timeout to 1 minute, endpoint auto-confirms to false, raw message delivery to false, filter/delivery policies to empty strings, and falling back to the created topic ARN when an explicit topic ARN override is omitted. The SMS preferences component must support monthly spend limits, delivery status IAM roles, success sampling rates, default sender IDs, default SMS types (Promotional or Transactional), and S3 bucket usage reporting. The platform application component requires a platform type and credential string, defaults its name to "lower(var.name)-sns-plat-app-{lower(var.environment)}", and supports event notifications for delivery failure, endpoint creation, deletion, or updates alongside success/failure feedback roles and sampling rates.

We need a Terraform template that creates a customizable Amazon EventBridge event processing module to route system events to target services. The module must accept dynamic inputs for an optional name variable defaulting to null (which uses a default naming module to fall back to "default" if null or empty), a tags map defaulting to empty, a bus configuration map defaulting to empty (which validates non-null input and supports an optional event_source_name parameter defaulting to null), a rules list defaulting to empty (which validates non-null input), and a targets list defaulting to empty (which validates non-null input). A custom EventBridge bus named after the module name must be conditionally created only when the name does not equal "default". EventBridge rules defined in the rules list must be generated using each rule's name key, inheriting optional parameters for description, event_pattern, and schedule_expression (defaulting to null), while attaching to the custom event bus if created. Additionally, provision an IAM role named "-invoke" assumed by the EventBridge service principal ("events.<dns_suffix>") with an inline policy named "-invoke-targets" permitting "lambda:InvokeFunction" and "states:StartExecution" across all resources. Finally, event targets defined in the targets list must be generated with explicit dependencies on the rules, linking each target's specified rule and ARN, attaching to the custom event bus if created, and dynamically assigning the created IAM role ARN only if the target ARN contains "stateMachine".

aws_services: aws_backup_plan, aws_backup_selection, aws_backup_vault, aws_backup_vault_notifications, aws_backup_vault_policy, aws_caller_identity, aws_iam_role, aws_iam_role_policy_attachment
user_prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a self-contained AWS Backup module with dynamic resource naming, customizable lifecycle rules, and IAM service permissions for automated backup orchestration. The module must provision an IAM role prefixed with "aws-backup-" assumed by the "backup.amazonaws.com" service principal attached to the managed AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup policy. The backup vault must be named using the prefix "vault-" followed by a name value and the suffix "-backup", accept an optional KMS key ARN, tag resources with a Job tag built from the name value followed by "-backup", and conditionally attach an access policy document when a vault policy variable is non-empty. The backup plan must be named using the prefix "plan-" followed by the name value and the suffix "-backup", tagged with the same Job tag pattern, and contain a rule named using the prefix "rule-" followed by the name value and the suffix "-backup" targeting the vault, with configurable schedule parameters (start window defaulting to 60 minutes, completion window defaulting to 120 minutes), recovery point tags using the same Job tag pattern, lifecycle transitions (cold storage after 30 days, deletion after 120 days), and dynamic copy actions mapped from a destination vault map variable defaulting to empty. The backup selection must be named using the prefix "selection-" followed by the name value and the suffix "-backup", linked to the created IAM role and plan, containing an empty condition block, and filtering resources via tag selection with operation type defaulting to "STRINGEQUALS", key defaulting to "Backup", and value defaulting to "true". Finally, the vault must conditionally configure event notifications when an SNS topic ARN variable is non-empty, defaulting subscribed events to "BACKUP_JOB_FAILED" and "COPY_JOB_FAILED".

We need a Terraform template that creates a modular, enterprise-grade Amazon EFS shared storage stack to support distributed container applications. Global prefix variables for name ("TEST") and environment ("STAGE") must construct default lowercased resource names when explicit names are omitted, and resource creation across components must be governed by individual boolean flags defaulting to false: enable_efs_file_system, enable_efs_mount_target, enable_efs_file_system_policy, and enable_efs_access_point. The EFS file system component must support configurable performance modes (defaulting to "generalPurpose"), encryption flags (defaulting to true), KMS key IDs, creation tokens, provisioned throughput levels, throughput modes, and dynamic lifecycle policy rules for transition to Infrequent Access storage while enforcing a create_before_destroy lifecycle policy. The mount target component must iterate across a list of subnet IDs defaulting to empty, supporting optional specific IP addresses and security groups, falling back to the created file system ID if an explicit file system ID is omitted. The file system policy component requires a JSON policy document, falling back to the created file system ID when an explicit ID is omitted. The access point component must support POSIX user permissions (UID, GID, secondary GIDs) and root directory configurations (path, creation info with owner UID/GID and permissions), automatically falling back to the created file system ID if an explicit file system ID override is not provided.

We need a Terraform template that creates a modular AWS CodeArtifact artifact management framework containing a domain, domain permissions policy, repository, and repository permissions policy for secure package management. Global prefix variables for name ("TEST") and environment ("STAGE") must construct default lowercased resource names when explicit names are omitted, and resource creation across components must be governed by individual boolean flags defaulting to false: enable_codeartifact_domain, enable_codeartifact_domain_permissions_policy, enable_codeartifact_repository, and enable_codeartifact_repository_permissions_policy. The CodeArtifact domain component must lower-case explicit domain names or fall back to "lower(var.name)-codeartifact-domain-{lower(var.environment)}", support custom KMS encryption key ARNs, merge a default Name tag with custom tags, and enforce a create_before_destroy lifecycle policy. The domain permissions policy component requires a JSON policy document, supports optional domain owner IDs and policy revisions, and automatically falls back to referencing the created domain name if an explicit domain name is not provided. The repository component lower-cases explicit repository names or falls back to "lower(var.name)-codeartifact-repository-{lower(var.environment)}", supports descriptions, domain owner IDs, upstream repository associations, external connection configurations, merges a default Name tag with custom tags, enforces create_before_destroy, and falls back to referencing the created domain name if an explicit domain name is omitted. The repository permissions policy component requires a JSON policy document, supports domain owner IDs and policy revisions, enforces create_before_destroy, and automatically falls back to referencing the created repository name and domain name when explicit overrides are omitted.

We need a Terraform template that creates a custom cross-account IAM role and policy integration to grant third-party security auditing platform access. The infrastructure must set up an IAM role whose name is configurable via a rolename variable defaulting to "WizAccess-Role", configured with an assume role policy that allows cross-account access to an AWS principal specified by a remote-arn variable defaulting to "arn:aws:iam::830522659852:role/prod-us43-AssumeRoleDelegator", constrained by a StringEquals condition on "sts:ExternalId" matching an external-id variable defaulting to "fc959d31-537c-4108-8b87-9af9e0c9b8d2". Attach the AWS-managed ViewOnlyAccess and SecurityAudit policies to the role, alongside an inline role policy named "WizCustomPolicy" that grants explicit permissions across seven distinct policy statements: read-only access across multiple services (ACM, API Gateway, Backup, CloudTrail, CodeBuild, Cognito Identity, Connect, DynamoDB, EC2, ECR, EKS, EFS, EMR, SSM, Glacier, Glue, Health, Kafka, Kendra, Kinesis Analytics/Video, KMS, Lambda, Logs, Amazon Profiles, S3, SES, VoiceID, WAFv2, Wisdom, Macie2, Identity Store, SSO Directory, CloudWatch metrics) on all resources; EBS snapshot creation and metadata retrieval actions (CopySnapshot, CreateSnapshot, GetEbsEncryptionByDefault, DescribeSnapshots) on all resources; tag creation on "arn:aws:ec2:::snapshot/"; KMS alias creation on "arn:aws:kms:::alias/wizKey" and "arn:aws:kms:::key/*"; KMS key policy actions (GetKeyPolicy, PutKeyPolicy) on all resources matching a resource tag condition of "aws:ResourceTag/wiz" equal to "auto-gen-cmk"; snapshot deletion and modification on all resources matching an EC2 resource tag condition of "ec2:ResourceTag/wiz" equal to "auto-gen-snapshot"; and an explicit Deny statement under statement ID "WizAccessS3" for "s3:GetObject" across all resources.

We need a Terraform template that creates configurable IAM roles for admin, poweruser, and readonly access levels to manage cross-account or service-based role assumption with optional MFA enforcement. The module should allow enabling or disabling each of the three roles independently, attaching specified lists of managed policy ARNs (defaulting to AdministratorAccess, PowerUserAccess, and ReadOnlyAccess respectively), and configuring custom role names, paths, permissions boundaries, max session durations, force detach policies behavior, and resource tags. Additionally, trust policies for these roles must dynamically construct assume role statements supporting specified principal ARNs and service identifiers, with conditional MFA checks enforced per role when enabled based on a maximum MFA age threshold that defaults to 86400 seconds.

We need a Terraform template that creates a flexible AWS Transit Gateway module to support central hub-and-spoke network routing and cross-account RAM sharing. The template must include a create boolean variable defaulting to true to toggle between provisioning a new Transit Gateway or looking up an existing one (via an id variable defaulting to null or filtering by a name tag defaulting to null). When creating the Transit Gateway, both default route table association and default route table propagation must be explicitly disabled, while allowing configuration of BGP ASN defaulting to 65200, auto_accept_shared_attachments, dns_support, vpn_ecmp_support, and transit_gateway_cidr_blocks (which validates that all entries are valid IPv4 or IPv6 CIDRs). Additionally, process a map of route_tables where each item conditionally creates a new Transit Gateway route table or looks up an existing one using a transit-gateway-id filter paired with a tag:Name filter, assigning route table tags from merged global tags, local_tags, and a fallback name tag equal to the table name or the main resource name. Finally, if a shared_principals map variable contains entries, provision an AWS RAM resource share that permits external principals, defaulting its share name to an explicit ram_resource_share_name variable or the main resource name, associate the Transit Gateway to the share, and attach each principal specified in the map.

user_prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a tiered AWS Backup architecture to manage automated snapshot retention across Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Premium service levels. The template must provision a shared KMS key with a 10-day deletion window and key rotation enabled, alongside an IAM role named "Bronze_Backup_Role" assumed by backup.amazonaws.com attached to the AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup and AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForRestores managed policies. Each service tier must feature a dedicated backup vault encrypted with the shared KMS key, a corresponding backup plan, and a resource assignment filtering resources where the tag key "Backup" equals the respective tier name using a STRINGEQUALS comparison. Specifically, the Bronze tier vault ("Bronze_Backup_Vault") must pair with the "Bronze_Backup" plan containing a weekly rule ("Bronze_Backup_Weekly") scheduled at "cron(0 0 ? * FRI *)" retaining backups for 10 days, assigned via "Bronze_Resource_Assignment". The Silver tier vault ("Silver_Backup_Vault") must pair with the "Silver_Backup_Plan" containing a daily rule ("Silver_Backup_Daily") scheduled at "cron(0 5 ? * * *)" retaining backups for 7 days, assigned via "Silver_Backup_resource". The Gold tier vault ("Gold_Backup_Vault") must pair with the "Gold_Backup" plan containing three rules—a daily rule ("Gold_Daily_Backup_Rule") at "cron(0 0 * * ? *)" retaining for 31 days, a monthly rule ("Gold_Monthly_Backup_Rule") at "cron(0 0 1 1/1 ? *)" retaining for 365 days, and a yearly rule ("Gold_Yearly_Backup_Rule") at "cron(0 0 31 12 ? *)" retaining for 2555 days—assigned via "Gold_Backup_Select". Finally, the Premium tier vault ("Premium") must pair with the "Premium" plan containing four rules—a 4-hour rule ("Premium_Daily_4Hour_Backup") at "cron(0 0/4 ? * * *)" retaining for 1 day, a daily rule ("Premium_Daily_Backup") at "cron(0 0 * * ? *)" retaining for 31 days, a monthly rule ("Premium_Monthly") at "cron(0 0 1 1/1 ? *)" transitioning to cold storage after 15 days and deleting after 365 days, and a yearly rule ("Premium_Yearly") at "cron(0 0 31 12 ? *)" transitioning to cold storage after 15 days and deleting after 2555 days—assigned via "Premium".

user_prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a data-driven, multi-function AWS Lambda execution environment configured via YAML inputs for serverless application deployment. The architecture must dynamically ingest function definitions either from a raw YAML configuration string variable defaulting to '"config": []' or, if empty, from a YAML configuration file path variable defaulting to "Path to the pipeline configuration file", extracting function parameters including function name, handler, runtime, source file path, architectures (defaulting to ["x86_64"]), code signing config ARN (defaulting to null), description (defaulting to empty), memory size (defaulting to 128 MB), timeout (defaulting to 3 seconds), environment variables, VPC subnets and security groups, custom IAM policy documents, CloudWatch log group names (defaulting to "/aws/lambda/"), and log retention periods (defaulting to 7 days). For every defined function, the template must provision an IAM role assumed by lambda.amazonaws.com using a configurable role name (defaulting to the function name) and path (defaulting to "/terrabits/lambda/"), attach an inline IAM policy if a custom policy document is supplied, generate a dedicated CloudWatch log group with the specified retention period, create an IAM logging policy named "<function_name>-logging" granting log creation and write permissions on "arn:aws:logs:::*" attached to the function role, and instantiate the Lambda function using base64 source hashes with dynamic VPC configurations applied when present while enforcing explicit dependencies on both the log group and logging policy attachment. Finally, all created resources must merge shared resource tags with an overarching tag setting Terraformed to true.

We need a Terraform template that creates a cross-account IAM role integration for Prisma Cloud security monitoring and compliance enforcement. The configuration must declare variables for an AWS region, an IAM role name defaulting to "PrismaCloudReadWriteRole", and a boolean flag named read_write defaulting to false. The template must generate a random 32-character alphanumeric external ID without special characters to configure the IAM role assume role policy, allowing assumption by the principal "arn:aws:iam::188619942792:root" conditioned on a StringEquals check against the generated external ID. Attach the managed SecurityAudit policy ("arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/SecurityAudit") to the role alongside an inline policy named "PrismaCloud-IAM-ReadOnly-Policy" that allows apigateway:GET, cognito-identity:ListTagsForResource, cognito-idp:ListTagsForResource, ecr:DescribeImages, ecr:GetLifecyclePolicy, elasticbeanstalk:ListTagsForResource, elasticfilesystem:DescribeTags, glacier:GetVaultLock, glacier:ListTagsForVault, glue:GetSecurityConfigurations, logs:GetLogEvents, mq:listBrokers, mq:describeBroker, ram:GetResourceShares, secretsmanager:DescribeSecret, ssm:GetParameters, ssm:ListTagsForResource, sqs:SendMessage, elasticmapreduce:ListSecurityConfigurations, sns:listSubscriptions, wafv2:ListResourcesForWebACL, and wafv2:ListWebACLs across all resources. Finally, conditionally create an inline remediation policy named "PrismaCloud-IAM-Remediation-Policy" attached to the role when read_write is true, allowing iam:UpdateAccountPasswordPolicy, ec2:ModifyImageAttribute, rds:ModifyDBSnapshotAttribute, s3:PutBucketAcl, and ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress across all resources.

provider "aws" {
  region = var.region
}

# Get the current account_id
data "aws_caller_identity" "current" {}

# Generate a random ExternalID for Prisma Cloud
resource "random_string" "external_id" {
  length  = 32
  special = false
}

# Create the IAM role for Prisma Cloud
resource "aws_iam_role" "prismacloud_role" {
  name               = var.role_name
  assume_role_policy = <<-EOF
  {
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Principal": {
          "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::188619942792:root"
        },
        "Action": "sts:AssumeRole",
        "Condition": {
          "StringEquals": {
            "sts:ExternalId": "${random_string.external_id.result}"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
  EOF
}

# Attach the SecurityAudit managed policy ARN
resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "prismacloud_role_policy_attachment" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.prismacloud_role.name
  policy_arn = "arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/SecurityAudit"
}

# Create and attach the ReadOnly inline policy
resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "prismacloud_iam_readonly_policy" {
  name   = "PrismaCloud-IAM-ReadOnly-Policy"
  role   = aws_iam_role.prismacloud_role.id
  policy = <<-EOF
  {
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Action": [
          "apigateway:GET",
          "cognito-identity:ListTagsForResource",
          "cognito-idp:ListTagsForResource",
          "ecr:DescribeImages",
          "ecr:GetLifecyclePolicy",
          "elasticbeanstalk:ListTagsForResource",
          "elasticfilesystem:DescribeTags",
          "glacier:GetVaultLock",
          "glacier:ListTagsForVault",
          "glue:GetSecurityConfigurations",
          "logs:GetLogEvents",
          "mq:listBrokers",
          "mq:describeBroker",
          "ram:GetResourceShares",
          "secretsmanager:DescribeSecret",
          "ssm:GetParameters",
          "ssm:ListTagsForResource",
          "sqs:SendMessage",
          "elasticmapreduce:ListSecurityConfigurations",
          "sns:listSubscriptions",
          "wafv2:ListResourcesForWebACL",
          "wafv2:ListWebACLs"
        ],
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Resource": "*"
      }
    ]
  }
  EOF
}

# Create and attach the Remediation inline policy if var.readwrite = true
resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "prismacloud_iam_remediation_policy" {
  count = var.read_write ? 1 : 0

  name   = "PrismaCloud-IAM-Remediation-Policy"
  role   = aws_iam_role.prismacloud_role.id
  policy = <<-EOF
  {
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
      {
        "Action": [
          "iam:UpdateAccountPasswordPolicy",
          "ec2:ModifyImageAttribute",
          "rds:ModifyDBSnapshotAttribute",
          "s3:PutBucketAcl",
          "ec2:RevokeSecurityGroupIngress"
        ],
        "Effect": "Allow",
        "Resource": "*"
      }
    ]
  }
  EOF
}

user_prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a flexible Amazon Route 53 hosted zone and DNS record management framework integrating Cloud Posse standard context labeling. The template must declare variables for hosted zone names (zone_name accepting a string or list of zone names), an explicit hosted zone ID (zone_id defaulting to null), a boolean flag to control private hosted zone creation (create_phz defaulting to false), a force_destroy flag defaulting to false, a list of associated VPC IDs (vpc_ids defaulting to empty), a boolean to enable DNSSEC signing (enable_dnssec defaulting to true), a default TTL defaulting to 3600 seconds, a global record overwrite flag (allow_overwrite defaulting to false), extra tags, and a complex list of record objects supporting optional fields for name, type, TTL, static records list, set_identifier, health_check_id, weight, failover type, and an alias configuration block containing target name, target zone_id, and evaluate_target_health boolean. Private hosted zones must be conditionally created when zone_name is provided and create_phz is true, dynamically attaching provided VPC IDs and ignoring lifecycle changes on associated VPCs. When hosted zones are created with enable_dnssec set to true, no VPC IDs provided, and create_phz is true, the template must provision an ECC_NIST_P256 KMS customer master key with a 7-day deletion window and key usage set to SIGN_VERIFY allowing dnssec-route53.amazonaws.com permissions, an associated Route 53 key signing key named using the zone name value followed by "-dnssec", and Route 53 hosted zone DNSSEC signing. Route 53 records must be generated either across created hosted zones or attached directly to the provided zone_id when hosted zone creation is skipped, automatically splitting TXT record strings exceeding 255 characters using double quotes, assigning the default TTL to non-alias records when an explicit TTL is absent, and dynamically configuring weighted, failover, or alias routing policies based on the input record attributes.

We need a Terraform template that creates a dual-mode Amazon ECR container registry module to manage private or public container image repositories for containerized application deployments. Resource creation must be governed by an overarching enable flag defaulting to true, alongside separate enable_private_ecr and enable_public_ecr boolean flags defaulting to false, configured with a shared repository_name variable defaulting to an empty string. The private repository component must support image tag mutability defaulting to "IMMUTABLE", force deletion defaulting to false, scan on push defaulting to true, encryption type defaulting to "KMS", optional custom KMS key ARN, configurable delete timeouts, and a lifecycle policy containing rule priority 1 to expire untagged images when exceeding max_untagged_image_count (defaulting to 1) and rule priority 2 to expire any images when total images stored exceed max_image_count (defaulting to 10). The public repository component must support optional catalog data configurations including about_text, architectures, description, logo_image_blob, operating_systems, and usage_text. Additionally, when either principals_readonly_access or principals_full_access list variables are populated, the template must construct and attach an IAM repository policy combining read-only access (granting ecr:* read actions for private or ecr-public:* read actions for public) as the source document and full access (granting ecr:* or ecr-public:*) as the override document.

Additionally, provision an internet gateway named "development-be-ig", a public route table named "development-be-public-rt" routing "0.0.0.0/0" traffic to the internet gateway and associated explicitly with the public subnet, and a security group named "http_access" with Name tag "development-be-sg" that permits SSH ingress on TCP port 22 restricted to "10.0.0.0/16", HTTP ingress on TCP port 80 open to "0.0.0.0/0", and all outbound egress traffic.

Standard public certificates require a validation method (defaulting to "DNS" and evaluated in uppercase), subject alternative names, optional transparency logging options, and enforce a create_before_destroy lifecycle policy. Private CA-issued certificates require a CA ARN, while imported certificates accept PEM-formatted private keys, certificate bodies, and optional certificate chains. The certificate validation component connects a target certificate ARN with validation record FQDNs and optional custom create timeouts. Finally, the ACM PCA component supports enabling status (defaulting to true), deletion retention windows in days, custom create timeouts, CA configurations (key algorithms, signing algorithms, and detailed subject identity attributes), and revocation CRL configurations (including expiration days, custom CNAMEs, enabled flags, and target S3 bucket names).

// File: main.tf
# This is the Quasar VPC layout.

locals {
  name = "dosomething-quasar"

  # NOTE: We share these resources between all environments.
  environment = "production"

  # These are all for our data stack.
  stack = "data"
}

# Quasar VPC IP Range:
resource "aws_vpc" "quasar_vpc" {
  cidr_block = "10.255.0.0/16"

  tags = {
    Name        = "Quasar"
    Application = local.name
    Environment = local.environment
    Stack       = local.stack
  }
}

# 1st RDS subnet for multi-AZ DB setup.
resource "aws_subnet" "subnet-a" {
  vpc_id     = aws_vpc.quasar_vpc.id
  cidr_block = "10.255.100.0/24"

  tags = {
    Name        = "Quasar RDS - 1A"
    Application = local.name
    Environment = local.environment
    Stack       = local.stack
  }
}

# 2nd RDS subnet for multi-AZ DB setup.
resource "aws_subnet" "subnet-b" {
  vpc_id     = aws_vpc.quasar_vpc.id
  cidr_block = "10.255.101.0/24"

  tags = {
    Name        = "Quasar RDS - 1E"
    Application = local.name
    Environment = local.environment
    Stack       = local.stack
  }
}

# Next 3 "bastion" blocks define rules for our bastion server
# as the only entry entry point for SSH'ing into our EC2 instances.
# Setup this way to reduce attach surface.
resource "aws_security_group" "bastion" {
  name        = "Quasar-Bastion"
  description = "22 from Everywhere"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.quasar_vpc.id

  tags = {
    Name        = "Quasar-Bastion"
    Application = local.name
    Environment = local.environment
    Stack       = local.stack
  }
}

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "bastion" {
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.bastion.id
  type              = "ingress"
  from_port         = 22
  to_port           = 22
  protocol          = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks       = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
}

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "bastion-egress" {
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.bastion.id
  type              = "egress"
  from_port         = 0
  to_port           = 0
  protocol          = "-1" # All protocols.
  cidr_blocks       = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
}

# Next 4 sections define security rules for our Jenkins instances. 
# The rules allow for SSH access from the "bastion" server defined above,
# and opens up port 8080 (default Jenkins port) to communicate with the "haproxy" 
# load-balancer section below that provides front-end routing and certificate
# management/decryption (now with Nginx instead of HA Proxy, similar to https://bit.ly/3gsjRo9).
resource "aws_security_group" "jenkins" {
  name        = "Quasar-Jenkins"
  description = "22 from Quasar-Bastion, 8080 from Quasar-HA-Proxy"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.quasar_vpc.id

  tags = {
    Name        = "Quasar-Jenkins"
    Application = local.name
    Environment = local.environment
    Stack       = local.stack
  }
}

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "jenkins-bastion" {
  security_group_id        = aws_security_group.jenkins.id
  type                     = "ingress"
  from_port                = 22
  to_port                  = 22
  protocol                 = "tcp"
  source_security_group_id = aws_security_group.bastion.id
}

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "jenkins-haproxy" {
  security_group_id        = aws_security_group.jenkins.id
  type                     = "ingress"
  from_port                = 8080
  to_port                  = 8080
  protocol                 = "tcp"
  source_security_group_id = aws_security_group.haproxy.id
}

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "jenkins-egress" {
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.jenkins.id
  type              = "egress"
  from_port         = 0
  to_port           = 0
  protocol          = "-1" # All protocols.
  cidr_blocks       = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
}

resource "aws_security_group" "haproxy" {
  name        = "Quasar-HA-Proxy"
  description = "80/443 Everywhere, 22 from Quasar Bastion"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.quasar_vpc.id

  tags = {
    Name        = "Quasar-HA-Proxy"
    Application = local.name
    Environment = local.environment
    Stack       = local.stack
  }
}

# The next 4 sections define load-balancer securty rules.
# The "haproxy" moniker is misleading and we now use Nginx for
# load-balancing similar details in https://bit.ly/3gsjRo9.
# Accepts 80/443 from the world and SSH access from "bastion".
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "haproxy-http" {
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.haproxy.id
  type              = "ingress"
  from_port         = 80
  to_port           = 80
  protocol          = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks       = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
}

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "haproxy-https" {
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.haproxy.id
  type              = "ingress"
  from_port         = 443
  to_port           = 443
  protocol          = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks       = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
}

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "haproxy-bastion" {
  security_group_id        = aws_security_group.haproxy.id
  type                     = "ingress"
  from_port                = 22
  to_port                  = 22
  protocol                 = "tcp"
  source_security_group_id = aws_security_group.bastion.id
}

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "haproxy-egress" {
  security_group_id = aws_security_group.haproxy.id
  type              = "egress"
  from_port         = 0
  to_port           = 0
  protocol          = "-1" # All protocols.
  cidr_blocks       = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
}

# Security groups for our ETL compute nodes.
# SSH access allowed from "bastion" and "Jenkins" since data pipeline
# runs happen on compute nodes instead of on Jenkins server itself.
resource "aws_security_group" "etl" {
  name        = "Quasar-ETL"
  description = "22 from Quasar-Bastion and Quasar-Jenkins"
  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.quasar_vpc.id

  tags = {
    Name        = "Quasar-ETL"
    Application = local.name
    Environment = local.environment
    Stack       = local.stack
  }
}

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "etl-bastion" {
  security_group_id        = aws_security_group.etl.id
  type                     = "ingress"
  from_port                = 22
  to_port                  = 22
  protocol                 = "tcp"
  source_security_group_id = aws_security_group.bastion.id
}

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "etl-jenkins" {
  security_group_id        = aws_security_group.etl.id
  type                     = "ingress"
  from_port                = 22

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "etl-egress" {

  cidr_blocks       = ["0.0.0.0/0"]

# Security rules for our RDS instance.
# TODO: Lockdown PostgreSQL to whitelist appropriate IP's only, e.g. from Fivetran, Looker, etc.
resource "aws_security_group" "rds" {
  name        = "Quasar-PostgreSQL"
  description = "Quasar PostgreSQL Connectivity"

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "rds" {

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "rds-etl" {

resource "aws_security_group_rule" "rds-egress" {

user_prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, production-grade Amazon S3 private storage bucket with automated compliance policy enforcement, lifecycle management, analytics, and optional inventory reporting. The template must accept a base bucket name defaulting to "benchmark-bucket-tf5x", with optional name prefixes based on the AWS IAM account alias when use_account_alias_prefix is enabled, or use a random suffix prefix when use_random_suffix is set to true. The bucket policy must extend any custom JSON bucket policy passed via custom_bucket_policy to enforce encrypted requests by denying s3:* actions over non-TLS transport ("aws:SecureTransport" equal to "false") and allow S3 service principals to write inventory and analytics data when bucket-owner-full-control ACL is specified. Bucket access blocks must be enabled by default (controlled by enable_s3_public_access_block) to restrict public ACLs and public bucket policies, while object ownership defaults to "BucketOwnerEnforced" under ownership control management. Server-side encryption must default to AES256 unless kms_master_key_id is provided to enable "aws:kms" encryption, with bucket_key_enabled defaulting to false. Versioning status must default to "Enabled", bucket force destroy defaults to false, transition default minimum object size is set to "all_storage_classes_128K", and lifecycle rules must automatically abort incomplete multipart uploads after 14 days while transitioning noncurrent versions to "STANDARD_IA" after 30 days and expiring them after 365 days. Storage class analytics defaulting to enabled (enable_analytics set to true) must write export data under prefix "_AWSBucketAnalytics/" with a 30-day lifecycle expiration, while optional bucket inventory (enable_bucket_inventory defaulting to false) writes ORC-formatted reports under prefix "_AWSBucketInventory/" on a "Weekly" schedule with a 14-day lifecycle expiration. Finally, logging to an external target bucket is conditionally enabled when logging_bucket is specified using a target prefix of "s3/" followed by the bucket's id and a trailing slash, transfer acceleration status is conditionally configured when transfer_acceleration is not null, bucket ACLs are applied when s3_bucket_acl is set, and CORS rules are dynamically applied from a cors_rules list.

To handle external traffic routing, create an Internet Gateway tagged igw-deploy-me, an Elastic IP allocated for VPC domain, and a NAT Gateway tagged deployme-natgw residing in the first private subnet that explicitly depends on the Internet Gateway. The architecture requires sixteen subnets partitioned logically into four distinct functional tiers: two private tiers of four subnets each, one public tier of four subnets configured to auto-assign public IPv4 addresses on launch, and one spare tier of four subnets. Configure custom routing tables for each tier: a main private route table tagged rt-private-deploy-me that routes 0.0.0.0/0 outbound traffic through the NAT Gateway and is explicitly set as the main route table for the VPC as well as associated with all eight private subnets across both private tiers; a public route table tagged rt-public-deploy-me that routes both IPv4 0.0.0.0/0 and IPv6 ::/0 traffic to the Internet Gateway and is associated with all four public subnets; and a spare route table tagged rt-spare-deploy-me that also routes IPv4 and IPv6 internet-bound traffic through the Internet Gateway and is associated with all four spare subnets. Finally, provision a security group named allow_web_traffic with tag allow_web_traffic that permits inbound HTTP (port 80), HTTPS (port 443), and SSH (port 22) from anywhere (0.0.0.0/0) alongside unrestricted outbound egress, and export the NAT Elastic IP's public IP address as a top-level output variable named server_public_ip.

When enabled and vault_name is provided, provision an AWS Backup Vault encrypted with an optional vault KMS key ARN, and conditionally create an SNS topic policy allowing backup.amazonaws.com to publish to a target topic alongside backup vault event notifications when a notifications map containing a sns_topic_arn is supplied. Finally, backup selections must attach to the plan using either the created or supplied IAM role ARN, combining single selection variables (selection_name, selection_resources, selection_not_resources, selection_conditions, selection_tags) with a selections list, supporting tag-based conditions including string_equals, string_like, string_not_equals, and string_not_like matches.

Inside this subnet, deploy the EC2 instance attached via a dedicated network interface configured to dynamically map a public IP on launch, while retaining the logic to optionally allocate and associate a static Elastic IP if requested. The instance must strictly enforce IMDSv2 and utilize a 20 GB encrypted root volume, with the flexibility to conditionally generate and attach an SSH key pair. For secure management, attach an IAM instance profile and role that trusts both the EC2 and SSM services, applying a dedicated IAM policy that explicitly grants SSM Session Manager permissions for control and data channels, alongside a toggleable option to attach the standard AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore managed policy. All deployed resources, including the compute instance, volumes, network interface, subnet, route table, and elastic IP, must adopt a standardized naming convention and tagging structure derived from project, application, environment, and availability zone prefixes, and the template must output the resulting ARNs and IDs of the EC2 instance, IAM role, instance profile, route table, and subnet.

user_prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a custom Amazon EKS cluster named "demo-eks" with unmanaged worker nodes deployed via a CloudFormation-managed Auto Scaling Group in the default VPC across three availability zones in us-east-1, ensuring the AWS provider applies a default tag of "kubernetes.io/cluster/demo-eks" set to "owned". First, provision the EKS control plane attached to the default VPC's public subnets, utilizing an IAM role named "eksClusterRole" that includes the standard EKS cluster and VPC resource controller policies. For the worker nodes, generate a 4096-bit RSA TLS private key, save it locally to "~/.ssh/eks-aws.pem", and register it as an AWS key pair named "eks_kp". Create a dedicated node security group allowing all outbound traffic, unrestricted internal communication between nodes, and tightly scoped TCP ingress and egress rules on ports 443 and 1025-65535 to permit two-way communication with the EKS control plane's security group. Provision an IAM role named "eks-demo-node" with managed policies for EKS worker nodes, CNI, ECR read-only, and SSM core management, and attach it to an instance profile. Next, configure an EC2 launch template using a t3.medium instance, a 30 GB gp2 root volume, optional IMDSv2 HTTP tokens with a hop limit of 2, the latest Amazon Linux 2 EKS-optimized AMI retrieved via SSM, and a base64-encoded user-data bootstrap script that connects to the cluster and signals a CloudFormation stack upon completion. After incorporating a 30-second delay to allow the launch template to settle, deploy a CloudFormation stack named "eks-cluster-stack" to provision the Auto Scaling Group across the public subnets with a minimum size of 1, desired capacity of 3, and maximum size of 4, ensuring it incorporates an update policy for rolling updates with a maximum batch size of 1, a minimum of 3 instances in service, and a 5-minute pause time. Finally, output the node instance role ARN, the node security group ID, and the newly created Auto Scaling Group ID returned directly by the CloudFormation stack.

Appended the account ID (via a new data.aws_caller_identity.replica_bucket_owner) to the bucket name, matching this project's established pattern for hardcoded-literal naming collisions. Verified with a full plan: 'Plan: 11 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy' (note: plan cannot verify S3 global-uniqueness itself, only a real apply can -- but an account-ID suffix is a well-established, effectively-guaranteed-unique pattern). Added a data.aws_caller_identity and appended the account_id to the primary bucket name too, matching the replica's own pattern.

user_prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a secure, highly durable remote state management architecture for multiple EKS stacks, utilizing an S3 backend in us-east-1 with cross-region replication to us-west-1. The deployment must provision a primary S3 bucket named dynamically with the AWS account ID, enforcing versioning, strict public access blocks, and a bucket policy that explicitly denies non-SSL requests. All objects in the primary bucket must be encrypted server-side by default using a new custom KMS key configured with a 7-day deletion window and automatic key rotation. For disaster recovery, provision a replica S3 bucket in the us-west-1 region with identical versioning, SSL enforcement, and public access blocks, secured by its own dedicated replica KMS key. Configure S3 cross-region replication on the primary bucket to automatically replicate KMS-encrypted objects to the replica bucket, attaching an IAM role with the precise permissions required to read the source objects, decrypt them using the primary KMS key, and encrypt them at the destination using the replica key. To support concurrent operations, iterate through a provided map of stack names and regions to deploy individual pay-per-request DynamoDB tables keyed by "LockID" for each stack's state locking, alongside dedicated IAM policies that grant stack-specific access to their respective DynamoDB table, S3 bucket prefix, and KMS key operations. Finally, the template must automatically generate a local "backend.tf" file for each stack within a relative "eks-stacks" directory to seamlessly integrate these backend configurations into our workflows, ensuring all created resources are tagged with a standardized set of state management labels.

user_prompt: We need a Terraform template that creates a comprehensive EKS-based application environment supported by external PostgreSQL, Redis, and S3 data services in us-east-1. The foundational network must consist of a custom VPC with a /16 CIDR block spanning two Availability Zones, featuring two public and two private /24 subnets, an internet gateway, and a route table allowing outbound internet access for the public subnets, alongside a unified security group permitting inbound traffic from anywhere on ports 22, 443, 5432, 6379, 6380, and 8201. For the container orchestration layer, deploy a version 1.31 EKS cluster associated with a dedicated IAM role containing cluster and VPC controller policies, and a managed node group of c4.2xlarge instances configured with a minimum of 1, a maximum of 3, and a desired capacity of 2 nodes, placed in the public subnets and attached to a node IAM role granting worker, CNI, ECR read-only, and full S3 access permissions. For the persistent data tier, provision a force-destroyable S3 storage bucket, a 400 GB PostgreSQL 14.24 RDS instance on a db.m5.xlarge node skipping final snapshots, and a single-node Redis 7.1 ElastiCache cluster using a cache.t3.small node type. Both the database and the cache must be placed into custom subnet groups mapped to the first public and first private subnets and secured by the unified security group. Finally, the template must expose outputs for the cluster name, deployment region, database endpoint, database name, administrative username, sensitive password, S3 bucket name, Redis host address, Redis port, and the AWS CLI command required to update the local kubeconfig.
